newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish privatisation board approves sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish privatisation board approves sell-offs.

text.p: Turkey's High Board of Privatisation has approved a series of sell-offs tendered in recent months which will raise approaching $600 million, officials said.
"A $600 million income has been secured for our Treasury," Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller was quoted as saying by Anatolian news agency after a meeting of the privatisation board.
Approval was given for the sale of state-owned Etibank which was broken into three last September and sold as three entities -- Etibank, Anadolubank and Denizbank -- for over $340 million.

The High Board also approved the sale of cement company Ergani Cimento for $47 million, tyre company Petlas for $36 million and maritime cargo company Deniz Nakliyat for $141 million, officials from the privatisation administration said.

"This is in reality giving control of all problems in the best way to the private sector...The private sector will be Turkey's driving force," Ciller was quoted as saying after Thursday evening's meeting.
The government has targeted privatisation revenues in 1997 of $5 billion as a key part of plans to balance the budget.
Ciller added that the process of selling state flat steel producer Eregli Demir Celik Fabrikalari A.S. (Erdemir) was continuing.

A tender last month for a 30-40 percent stake in Erdemir drew only two bids. The government holds a 51.66 percent stake in Erdemir, one of the most actively traded companies on the Istanbul stock market.
